Question_text: In this experiment, you will determine the frictional force opposing the motion of a block of wood up a ramp. You are provided with a ramp with a stop close to its upper end, a pulley arrangement, a block of wood labelled A, with a small hook, a 10 g slotted mass hanger, nine 10 g slotted masses and two 100 g slotted masses, string passing over the pulley, with loops attached to the block and the mass hanger, a stopwatch, a metre rule, a set square.
image: Fig. 3.1 shows a ramp setup. A wooden block labeled 'A' with a hook is positioned at the top of the ramp, touching a stop. A string runs from the block, over a pulley at the top of the ramp, and down to a mass hanger with masses. The ramp rests on a bench, and the mass hanger hangs towards the floor. The vertical height 'h' of the ramp's top edge and the distance 's' along the ramp are indicated. Fig. 3.2 shows a similar ramp setup, but the block 'A' is placed at the bottom of the ramp, attached to the mass hanger over the pulley.

Measure the vertical height h and the distance s along the ramp, as shown in Fig. 3.1. Give your answers in metres. h = ____ m s = ____ m
